title: The design-tool helper
scenario: The studio links a design-tool server to its AI app. You choose which tools to switch on. Use the exhibit. The tool lines are copied from Figma's docs. The asks and the third-party server are made up for this case.
exhibit:
TOOLS ON THE DESIGN SERVER (names and lines copied from Figma's tool list):
  READ
    get_design_context     Design context for a layer or selection
    get_screenshot         Screenshot of a selection
    get_variable_defs      Variables and styles used in a selection
    search_design_system   Searches libraries for components, variables, styles
    whoami                 Identity and plans of the authenticated user
  WRITE
    use_figma              General-purpose create, edit, and inspect
    create_new_file        Creates a blank Design, FigJam, or Slides file
    upload_assets          Uploads images into a Figma file
    generate_image         Generates a downloadable raster image

STUDIO ASKS (made up for this case):
  Ask A  Read the approved brand frame and list the colour variables it uses.
  Ask B  Make a new file with three layout ideas for the autumn banner.
  Ask C  Fix typos on the 40 live client files, all at once, by itself.

A THIRD-PARTY SERVER (made up for this case):
  The studio also tests a small server from an unknown author. One of its
  tools has an annotation that says it is read-only.

questions.prompt: What does Ask A need from the design server?

options.text: Only read tools, such as get_variable_defs, because no write tool is needed for this job
options.explanation: Right. Listing variables only takes information out of Figma. A read job needs read tools only.

options.text: Only use_figma, because it is the general tool and so it can also look at a file
options.explanation: use_figma is listed under write tools. It can change files, so it is more than this job needs.

options.text: The whole list, because the server only works when every tool is switched on together
options.explanation: Nothing says that. You can choose which tools the model sees.

options.text: upload_assets and get_screenshot, so the agent can compare a picture with the frame
options.explanation: upload_assets writes images into a file. A read job needs no upload.

questions.prompt: On Claude's MCP connector, how do you make sure only the read tools are on?

options.text: Write in the system prompt that the agent must not edit anything in any client file
options.explanation: A prompt line is a request, not a setting. A tool that is on can still be called.

options.text: Switch every tool off by default, then turn on only the named read tools, one by one
options.explanation: Right. Claude's connector supports an allowlist. Anthropic also recommends denylisting write tools for read-only work.

options.text: Leave every tool on, because the tool hints tell Claude which ones are safe to use
options.explanation: Hints are untrusted unless they come from a trusted server. They are not a control.

options.text: Use OpenAI's allowed_tools setting inside the Claude request to name the read tools
options.explanation: allowed_tools is OpenAI's setting. Claude's connector has its own allowlist and denylist.

questions.prompt: What is the best plan for Ask C, the typo fix on the 40 live client files?

options.text: Switch on use_figma now, because fixing a typo is a small change that is easy to undo
options.explanation: Small changes on 40 live files still add up. A person should stay able to deny each write.

options.text: Switch on every write tool and trust the agent, since Ask C says it should work by itself
options.explanation: The MCP spec says there should always be a human in the loop with the ability to deny.

options.text: Ask the model in the prompt to be careful, then run all 40 files in one single batch
options.explanation: Care in a prompt is not a control. A batch on live files raises the risk.

options.text: Begin in Look, then test one write on a copy of a file, with a person approving each one
options.explanation: Right. The spec says a human should be able to deny tool calls. Anthropic suggests a confirmation step before state changes.

questions.prompt: A tool on the unknown author's server has an annotation that says it is read-only. Do you rely on it?

options.text: Yes, because a read-only hint means the tool cannot change anything in the studio files
options.explanation: A hint is only the server's claim about itself. It does not prove anything.

options.text: Yes, but only after the model has read the hint aloud to the person who approves the tool
options.explanation: Reading a hint aloud does not test it. The server still has to be trusted.

options.text: Not on its own, since hints are untrusted unless the server is trusted, so check the server
options.explanation: Right. The MCP spec says clients must treat tool annotations as untrusted unless they come from trusted servers.

options.text: No, because MCP forbids a tool from carrying hints, so the field must be an error
options.explanation: MCP allows annotations. The rule is about how much to trust them.
